doc: The OpenInference dialect. Its indexed message families are still read in Rust, deliberately: `enrich_oi_multimodal_from_input_value` rebuilds multimodal content blocks from a LangChain-serialised `input.value` and operates on the messages that extractor itself produced, so declaring the families here would leave rules a Rust extractor shadows - dead data, which is the defect the contested-carrier check refuses one level down. They move when that enrichment has a primitive.

carriers.doc: What this span produced, as an indexed array.

The conversation this span received, as an indexed array. Its members are separate attribute keys that are one array, so they carry an ordering family: `llm.input_messages.0.message` and `.1.message` are one sequence, and the order resolver needs to know that to sequence a request's own new turns. That fact used to be a hardcoded key comparison in the resolver, which is precisely the shape of framework knowledge this engine exists to hold instead.

detect.doc: The generic OpenInference dialect, after every framework that rides on it.
detect.label: OpenInference

messages.doc: The query a reranker was given, as prose. Carries a literal `_source` naming which carrier it came from, which is how the pipeline tells two role-`user` messages of a rerank span apart.
The text an embedding span was given, under the same reading.
